newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico church protests arrest of Jesuit priests.
newsitem.headline: Mexico church protests arrest of Jesuit priests.
newsitem.dateline: SAN CRISTOBAL DE LAS CASAS, Mexico 1997-03-09

text.p: Mexico's Roman Catholic church said on Sunday two of its Jesuit priests had been wrongly arrested, beaten and charged with leading a deadly ambush against police in the troubled southern state of Chiapas.
Police arrested Gonzalo Rosas and Geronimo Hernandez on Saturday afternoon in the tourist city of Palenque, some 90 miles (150 km) east of the state capital Tuxtla Gutierrez.
Two local Mayan Indian leaders, identified as Francisco Gonzalez and Ramon Parcero, were also arrested, a state spokesman told Reuters.

All four men were charged with taking part on Friday in an ambush of state police who hours earlier forcibly removed peasants from farms they had illegally occupied. In the ambush two policemem were killed and five others injured.

But the diocese in San Cristobal de las Casas, some 60 miles (100 km) west of Palenque, contradicted the police version of events, saying the two priests were in this colonial city at the time of the ambush after having taken part in a religious conference.
Church officials said the two men were beaten by police in jail and had been kept from seeing their lawyers.

"The priests were beaten during their detention and until now have remained incommunicado ... except for a brief visit this morning by two diocese officials who confirmed the pair had suffered psysical abuse," Gonzalo Ituarte, vicar general at the diocese, told Reuters.

Dozens of plainclothes and uniformed police violently yanked the pair from their car in Palenque on Saturday, Ituarte said. Police showed no arrest warrant and have since added false weapons possesion charges against one of the priests, he added.
Tensions flared on Friday after hundreds of armed police removed peasants from two local collective farms they had occupied since 1994, police said in a statement.

Hours later, the peasants, members of a local Indian rights group called "Xi-Nich" (meaning ant in Chol dialect), blocked a local highway to protest the police operation and demand the release of several of their arrested comrades.
Police said they peacefully broke up the protest and were later ambushed by the priests and two Xi-Nich leaders.
But the Xi-Nich said in a statement on Sunday that police, backed by helicopters, began firing at the highway protesters, who fired back.

The incident was likely to further sour already bitter relations between the church and local officials in Chiapas. Controversial Bishop Samuel Ruiz has for decades worked with Chiapas' marginalized Indians, but been accused by officials and wealthy local landowners of fostering rebellion by encouraging land takeovers.
